summary.text: 尾道ラーメン（おのみちラーメン）は、尾道市を中心とした広島県備後地方のご当地ラーメン。
summary.license: CC BY-SA 4.0

summary.text: 広島ラーメン（ひろしまラーメン）とは、戦後の広島市を中心とする広島県西部に散見される醤油とんこつ味のラーメン（中華そば）である。
summary.license: CC BY-SA 4.0

summary.text: Sake hot pot is a simple dish made by cooking chicken, gizzard, pork, and vegetables with a straightforward seasoning of salt, pepper, and sake. It's light and lets you enjoy the natural flavors of the ingredients. It's said to have originated as a staff meal invented by a sake brewer in Nishijo, Hiroshima City, to satisfy hunger during breaks from sake-making. The simple seasoning is designed to not affect the ability to taste sake.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Tai-men is a dish featuring boiled somen noodles piled in waves on a large plate and topped with a whole boiled sea bream, garnished with prickly ash leaves, cucumber, shredded egg crepe, and salty-sweet simmered shiitake mushroom. It can also be garnished with pine branches. It is a ceremonial dish often served for special occasions such as house framing ceremonies, 77th birthdays, 88th birthdays, weddings, and ship unloading ceremonies.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: The vegetarian dish "Nigome" is made with diced and boiled azuki beans, daikon radish, carrots, dried shiitake mushrooms, burdock root, lotus root, taro, deep-fried tofu, and konjac. No meat or fish is used in the ingredients or broth. The western part of the prefecture is called "Aki no Kuni" and has many Jodo Shinshu followers, who were named "Aki followers". Shinran Shonin, the founder of the Jodo Shinshu sect, passed away on January 16th, which is celebrated as "Goshoiki".
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

name.en: Igisu tofu (Red algae and soy flour)

summary.text: This dish is made from a type of algae called “igisu”, which is mixed with raw soy flour and heated until it melts, then set like gelatin. It works on the same principle as vegetable gelatin or agar-agar, and sets without any need to add a coagulant. It is always made for Bon festival or other occasions when friends and family gather. In some areas it is frequently made during summer. The garnishes and seasonings used vary depending on the region and the household. In summer it is eaten chilled from the fridge.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

name.en: Kuwai no Ama-ni (Arrowhead simmered in a sweet sauce)

summary.text: Kuwai no Ama-ni is a stew that is known for its sweet taste, which is seasoned with broth, sugar, and mirin. The dish is named after "kuwaimo," a potato-like fruit that grows under the leaves shaped like a hoe for digging up the earth. There are three types of arrowhead: ao kuwai (blue arrowhead), shiroi kuwai (white arrowhead), and suita kuwai. Ao kuwai, the main type grown in Japan, is characterized by its round, spherical shape and vivid blue surface.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Kinako-musubi is a round omusubi with dried plums and thinly sliced salted kelp, covered with kinako (roasted soybean flour). It was served between rice plantings and at the end of the rice planting season called “dai-mite”. In Hiroshima, "Mite" means "disappear,” and Kinako musubi along with "Bara Sushi" and "Grilled Mackerel Chishamomi" are eaten. It is said that the sushi was made in a round shape with the wish that the seedlings planted would bear a full crop in the fall.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Nebuto is a white-fleshed fish of 3 to 5 cm caught mainly in the Seto Inland Sea, and is commonly called tenjikudai. It is also called "ishimochi" or "ishikaberi" because of its hard head. Because its otolith bone is larger than those of other fish, it cannot be eaten whole from the head even though it is a small fish, so the head is removed and eaten.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: It is a type of oshizushi made by filling a square wooden mold with sushi rice and other ingredients, and is eaten in the Asakita-ku area of Hiroshima City and the Geihoku region of Hiroshima Prefecture. When pressed out of the wooden frame, six to eight pieces of the same size are formed at the same time, and the finished product is square, hence the name "kaku-zushi" (square sushi). It is sometimes called "oshizushi" or "Inaka sushi" (country sushi).
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

name.en: Ko-iwashi no sashimi (sashimi of small sardine)

summary.text: "Ko-iwashi" refers to Japanese anchovy, and has long been known as "small sardines" in Hiroshima Prefecture. Hiroshima Bay is rich in plankton, which serves as bait for small sardines, so well grown sardines are caught in abundance.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: "Takomeshi" is octopus cooked with rice. Originally, fishermen would chop octopus on the boat and cook it into rice and eat it as fishermen's rice. The environment off the coast of Mihara is particularly suitable for growing octopus because of its good water quality, stable water temperature, and rocky areas with abundant bait, and octopus fishing has been popular since the Edo period. Even today, the Seto Inland Sea is one of the most important habitats for octopus.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Mama Kari Sushi is a type of nigiri sushi made with fish that has been marinated in vinegar. The distinctive feature is the use of okara (soy pulp) seasoned with vinegar instead of vinegared rice. In the past, when rice was scarce, okara, which was more readily available, was used as a substitute to conserve rice. This type of sushi is not limited to Mama Kari; it can also be made with fish such as Kohada (gizzard shad) or Konoshiro (dotted gizzard shad).
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: It is called "crocodile", but what is actually eaten is "shark". It is also called "fuka. In the mountainous areas of the Chugoku region, there is an old word for "shark" called "crocodile," and the crocodile that appears in the myth "Inaba no Shirohagi (White Hare of Inaba)" in the Kojiki is also thought to be a shark. There is a record of sharks being brought to this area from merchants on the Sea of Japan coast during the Edo period (1603-1868).
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

name.en: Kure-no-Nikujaga (Kure style Meat and Potato Stew)

summary.text: In the case of the general "nikujaga" (meat and potato stew), it typically consists of potatoes, beef, and onions as the main ingredients, with variations in additional vegetables such as carrots and snap peas, all seasoned with soy sauce and sugar. However, "Kure's Nikujaga" features the use of "May Queen" potatoes, along with standard ingredients like beef, shirataki (konjac noodles), and onions. The unique aspect is that it is prepared with a fixed set of ingredients.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: "Ebiko" is made by peeling and finely chopping boiled small shrimp (Akaebi) with a knife, and then sweetening and stir-frying them with sugar, mirin, sake, etc. Some people use a mortar and pestle instead of a knife.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Traditional nori(seaweed) rolls from the Eba district in the central area of Hiroshima City, where nori cultivation has been thriving for a long time. This type of nori roll has been consumed since ancient times. It consists of rice, Hiroshima-style pickled vegetables, bonito flakes, soy sauce, and sesame seeds mixed together, then rolled and wrapped with roasted seaweed. Instead of vinegar rice, regular rice is used, and the filling includes pickled vegetables and other easily preserved ingredients.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

name.en: Hiroshima-nazuke-no Onigiri (Rice ball wrapped in pickled Hiroshima mustard)

summary.text: Rice ball wrapped in pickled Hiroshima mustard. Hiroshima-na is a type of Chinese cabbage belonging to the Brassicaceae family. Sown in September, it grows well in December, and the frost gives it a tangy flavor. It is said that the seeds were brought back from Kyoto during the Edo period (1603-1867), and many elderly people call it kyona (meaning Kyoto vegetable), suggesting that it has its roots in Kyoto's mibuna. Because of the shape of its stem, it is also called Hira-guki (flat stem). The name Hiroshima-na was given in 1933.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Fish rice is a dish consisting of grilled and loosened white fish topped with colorful ingredients such as kinshi tamago (thin cut omelets), mitsuba, shiitake mushrooms, shrimp, seaweed, and bamboo shoots, and served on rice with soup made from the bones. The city of Takehara, where the dish is mainly handed down, used to be a shallow sea, but it was reclaimed during the Edo period (1603-1868) and salt fields were built, and it flourished as a salt town for more than 320 years from 1650 to 1970.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: It is a traditional stew in Otake City. Root vegetables such as satoimo (Japanese taro), lotus root, carrot, daikon radish, gobou (burdock root), chicken, konjac (yam cake), dried shiitake mushrooms, and thick fried tofu are cut into pieces or bite-sized pieces, seasoned with dashi (Japanese soup stock), soy sauce, sugar, etc., and then simmered. The name ohira is said to come from the large, flat bowl in which it is placed when served on a table.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Stir-fried julienned daikon radish, fried thin tofu, nebuka-negi (Japanese leeks), and iriko (dried sardines) in soy sauce seasoning. Because it is cooked using only the water from the ingredients, the flavor is not lost and the dish is rich. Although the word boiled is in the name, it is similar to stir-fried food. It was loved by busy farmers as an everyday side dish that could be prepared quickly, deliciously, and in large quantities. In the northern part of Fukuyama City, it is called nija and in the southern part, nizai.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

name.en: Kaki Zoni (Japanese Soup made with Rice Cakes and Oysters)

summary.text: "Kaki zoni" is a "sumashi-jiru" (=clear soup) made with dried sardines, kombu (=kelp), and bonito soup stock. The soup contains oysters, yellowtail, and vegetables. Sometimes, miso is used for the soup. Yellowtail is fatty and remains fresh for a long time, which is why it is used for "zoni" eaten during the New Year holidays. An entire yellowtail is used to make sashimi and "zoni" with the leftover fish.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: "Kaki meshi" is a mixed rice made with oysters from aquaculture in the areas around Etajima city. The local people of Hiroshima have been eating oysters for a long time. Shell middens have shown that wild oysters were eaten as far back as the Jomon and Yayoi periods. It is believed that aquaculture of oysters began between the 1500s and 1600s.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: もち米や米の粉で作った皮で小豆のあんを包み、鮮やかに彩ったもち米の粒を上に乗せて蒸したお菓子。もちもちとした食感と上に乗ったもち米の粒々とした食感が楽しめる。亀山神社の例大祭と小祭りといった秋祭りの時期になると菓子店や屋台などで販売され、屋台では蒸したてのものを楽しむこともできる。名前の由来は「栗のイガに似ているから」や「旅の僧侶が食べたところ胃の病が治ったことから、胃が持つ（治る）から」など様々な説がある。
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Uzumi" is said to have originated in the Edo period (1603-1867), when people buried the ingredients under the rice to make it look more simple. Shrimp, sea bream, taro and other vegetables cooked in broth are placed in a bowl, and rice is served on top of the broth. In the Chugoku region, there are other "burying" food cultures outside of Fukuyama City, such as "Uzume-meshi" in the Iwami region of Shimane Prefecture and "Bizen-bara-zushi" in Okayama Prefecture. Until the 1960s, it was often eaten as a dish to celebrate the autumn harvest.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Grilled conger eel is cut into smaller pieces and placed on top of warm rice cooked with dashi (=Japanese soup stock). Sometimes, the conger eel is steamed. Conger eels are caught in Miyajima Town and Hiroshima city and the local people have been eating them over a long time. "Geihan Tsushi," a geographical journal written during the Bunsei era of the Edo period by the Hiroshima Domain in Aki Province, describes conger eels along with "mebaru" (=Japanese red seaperch), and smelt as delicious fish from the region.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Hachisun" is a stew made from a combination of mountain and sea vegetables that was eaten in areas where there were many Aki Monzoku (Jodo Shinshu sect members in the western part of Hiroshima Prefecture). Some say that the name comes from the fact that the lacquerware used to serve it has a diameter of eight inches (about 24 centimeters), while others say that it is made from "eight different ingredients. It is also called "ohasun.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: There are three origins of the name of "oyster Dote-nabe". The first is that miso is coated on the inside of the pot like a bank. The second is that Chokichi Dote was the inventor of this nabe dish. The third is said to be because oyster boats that transported oysters from Hiroshima to Osaka during the Edo period served the nabe on the river bank. The characteristic feature of this way of eating is that the taste is adjusted by breaking up the miso paste coated on the edge of the nabe.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: It is a hybrid of leek and shallot, and has a unique aroma different from that of green onions. It is a member of the leek family, but has a unique aroma that is different from that of green onions. It is called "wakaegi," meaning "a leek whose root is divided into many plants. The Seto Inland Sea coast has a mild climate suitable for growing wekegi, and Onomichi in particular boasts the nation's largest production (Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries "Survey of Regional Specialty Vegetable Production in Fiscal Year 2008").
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: The name "Moburi" is derived from the Hiroshima dialect, meaning "to mix" or "to blend." Depending on the region, it is also known as "Mōburi-gohan" or "Moguri-meshi." Moburi is a dish where cooked rice is mixed with various vegetables such as dried shiitake mushrooms, burdock root, carrots, black beans, and snow peas. It can also include cooked or grilled seafood such as shrimp, fish, or clams, and instead of black beans, other beans like pinto beans may be used. The ingredients vary depending on the region and season.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: The okonomiyaki made in Hiroshima is a dish wherein thinly spread batter is cooked in a pan and piled with heaps of cabbage, pork, yakisoba, a thinly fried egg, or other ingredients. While topping it with a rich, sweet sauce is universal, mayonnaise is also often added if you like. A spatula is used as the eating utensil when okonomiyaki is eaten from the steel plate griddle it’s cooked on.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: “Taimeshi” is a local dish mainly eaten in the Seto Inland Sea coastal region. It’s made by putting a whole sea bream in a pot and cooking it with rice. It’s said that fishermen began making this dish during the Edo period when the village headman of Hashirishima started casting a sea bream fishing net. The Seto Inland Sea is characterized by a rocky and undulating seabed terrain, along with strong tidal currents, making it a suitable spawning environment and habitat for sea bream.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）
